name: Autosomal Recessive Isolated Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse, symmetric hyperkeratosis on palms and soles
Confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance pattern by family history or genetic testing
Lack of additional ectodermal, neurological, or systemic abnormalities
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with no epidermolytic changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with autosomal recessive inheritance and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and exclusion of other keratodermas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse symmetric hyperkeratosis of palms and soles
pathognomonic.notes: Thickened, yellowish plaques covering entire palmoplantar surfaces
searchTerms: symmetrical thickened skin on palms and soles
evenly distributed palm and sole calluses
diffuse hyperkeratosis on hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early childhood onset of palmoplantar keratoderma
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents within first decade of life
searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles starting early
early onset thick skin on hands and feet
childhood palm and sole skin thickening

common.symptomName: Fissuring and painful cracks in hyperkeratotic skin
common.notes: May cause discomfort and secondary infections
searchTerms: painful cracks in thickened skin
fissuring with discomfort in callused areas
splitting and pain in hyperkeratotic skin

palm and sole sweating
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

erythema beneath keratoderma areas
redness under callused skin

common.symptomName: Nail dystrophy including thickening and ridging

nail changes including thickening and lines

bacterial or fungal infections on affected areas
infected keratoderma lesions

occasional.notes: Related to fissuring and thickened skin

rare.symptomName: Mild hyperkeratosis of elbows or knees
rare.notes: Rare extension beyond palms and soles
searchTerms: mild thickening of skin on elbows or knees
slight hyperkeratosis at joints

blistering that resolves in infancy

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing compact hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes
genetic: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with autosomal recessive palmoplantar keratoderma (e.g., SLURP1 mutations)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis on histology
Associated ectodermal, neurological, or systemic abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Signs of systemic involvement (neurological, cardiac, or renal symptoms)
Family history suggestive of syndromic keratoderma
references: Rajpopat S, Moss C, Mellerio J, et al. Clinical and genetic characterization of autosomal recessive palmoplantar keratoderma. J Invest Dermatol. 2011;131(4):865-868.
